title: #042. Solution Uniqueness via No-Good Cuts
subtitle: Add a blocking no-good clause after finding a satisfying assignment to prove whether a SAT solution is unique.

judge.m0: Output must be an object { satisfiable, assignment, unique }.
judge.m1: When satisfiable is false, assignment must be null.
judge.m2: An unsatisfiable formula cannot have unique = true.
judge.m3: Formula is satisfiable, yet output returned satisfiable: false.
judge.m4: Rule {p0} evaluated to false under the returned assignment.
judge.m5: Returned unique = true, but at least two distinct satisfying assignments exist.
judge.m6: Returned unique = false, but the satisfying assignment is provably unique.
judge.m9: Verified satisfiable with multiple distinct solutions (unique = false).
